targets.self_route_holds: the not-ready outcome holds; the stated reason (contact guard unmet) is a symptom of a PAG-freeze lock that is PROVABLE from the gate's own rule and the recorded latent: post-p0 ||z_harm_a|| = 2.8-4.2, so with duration 1 the commit value exceeds theta_freeze 0.8 on tick 1 of every life; exit requires ||z_harm_a|| < 0.8 (gaba_tone 1.0) and max_freeze_duration is 0 (never). The action is overridden to STAY inside select_action (agent.py ~11526-11548). Pinned env seeds put every eval life on the same hazard-adjacent spawn, which is why all 15 lives are identical; the lock is why the agent never leaves. A blind re-queue would reproduce it.

facts.collapse: probe lives: init 6-22 steps; p0/hazard/p1/p2 exactly 6 on all 3 seeds; final eval 6 x 15 in both arms; every life ends at harm ~-1.0..-1.26 (health depletion), so a 6-step life = the agent at a hazard from spawn, never leaving. facts.deltas_vs_935a: 935a ran the same freeze-gate settings (theta 0.8, duration threshold 0.2, harm pathway trained) on PRE-fix code, where a frozen agent walked UP one cell per tick -- which is how a permanently frozen agent still logged contacts. GFLAG-0508 (open) lists 935/935a among affected runs. So 935a is NOT a validated healthy baseline, and 1fc881692d UNMASKED the lock rather than caused it. Env-seed pinning (ENV_SEED_BASE 1107, reaching the training scheduler) explains the identical lives, not the failure to leave.

learning_extracted: The PAG freeze gate's fixed theta (0.8) is far below the trained ||z_harm_a|| scale (2.8-4.2) and it has no release: the freeze-gated harness locks from tick 1. Pre-fix, the lock was masked by UP-walking; 1fc881692d unmasked it (GFLAG-0508).

A constant latent across ticks can be an encoder saturation, not stationarity; argue stationarity from the controller's rule.
